speaker: Leonard Tran
cascadeSummary: I support a recorded YES vote on Downtown Economic Revitalization, with formal Chinatown and Uptown appropriation tracks and public timeline and transit-access information. I will vote YES on Grand Lake with its milestone and audit conditions intact. For Baylight, I support the scheduled evidence review but will not call the construction milestone passed before its findings are published.

statements.decision: Vote YES on INIT-008, with formalized appropriation tracks for Chinatown and Uptown and public timeline and transit-access planning.
statements.quote: I support the investment, but the public should be able to see where the money is assigned and how people will reach the corridors it serves.
statements.fullStatement: I support a binding vote on Downtown Economic Revitalization and will vote YES. That support comes with a clear expectation: formalize and publish the appropriation tracks for Chinatown and Uptown, along with the timeline and transit-access planning. Chinatown's mood has soured even as street trade remains busy and crime is low; that deserves a concrete, transparent response, not an inflated emergency claim. The packet does not provide D2 neighborhood mapping, so I will not present either Chinatown or Uptown as my district turf. I am asking for the public record to make the proposed allocations and implementation schedule inspectable.
statements.actionAsked: Record the full-council vote and publish the Chinatown and Uptown appropriation tracks, timeline, and transit-access planning.

statements.decision: Vote YES with all Chen-Vega milestone reporting and audit conditions intact.
statements.quote: A low-severity improvement is encouraging; it is not a reason to drop the reporting that lets the public judge the work.
statements.fullStatement: I will vote YES on Commercial Stabilization for Grand Lake, with every milestone and audit condition intact. The current review flags improvement at low severity, which is a positive sign, but it does not replace the need to report progress and account for the use of the $2.5 million. A recorded decision gives the public a clear commitment to assess rather than an open-ended promise. I want the required reporting to remain part of the initiative as it moves forward.
statements.actionAsked: Record the full-council decision and retain all milestone reporting and audit conditions.

statements.decision: Conduct the C115 construction milestone review against the assembled evidence file and publish findings before declaring whether the milestone passed.
statements.quote: The evidence file is ready for review; the milestone is not earned until the findings say so.
statements.fullStatement: The C115 review should proceed against the assembled evidence file, and its findings should be made public. The record describes independent remediation verification, hotline and dust-control records, and Jack London workforce results as assembled; it does not give me the review's findings. I will not call the construction milestone passed before that review is complete. Jack London's mood has slipped, so the workforce results matter, but I will not assume what they show or claim Jack London as D2 turf when the packet supplies no district mapping.
statements.actionAsked: Complete and publish the C115 evidence review before declaring the construction milestone passed.
